name: Infectious Anterior Uveitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Infectious Anterior Uveitis

criteria.description: Presence of inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber on slit-lamp examination
Detection of keratic precipitates on the corneal endothelium
Laboratory or PCR confirmation of infectious etiology (e.g., herpes simplex virus, cytomegalovirus, tuberculosis)
Symptoms such as eye redness, photophobia, and decreased vision

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anterior chamber inflammatory cells and keratic precipitates with clinical signs consistent with anterior uveitis; laboratory confirmation of infectious agent supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires exclusion of non-infectious causes and may be supported by response to antimicrobial therapy.

searchTerms: inflammatory cells in front eye chamber
white blood cells in anterior chamber

occasional.symptomName: Hypopyon (layered white blood cells in anterior chamber)
searchTerms: pus layer in front eye chamber
white blood cell layering in eye

rare.symptomName: Posterior synechiae (adhesions between iris and lens)

searchTerms: cloudy lens after surgery or trauma

laboratory: PCR detection of viral DNA (e.g., HSV, CMV, VZV) in aqueous humor
Positive serology for infectious agents (e.g., syphilis, tuberculosis)
Elevated inflammatory markers in aqueous humor
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing anterior chamber inflammation
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating inflammatory cells
other: Response to antimicrobial or antiviral therapy supports infectious etiology

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of infectious agent on laboratory testing
Better response to corticosteroids without antimicrobials
Corneal dendritic ulcers visible on fluorescein staining
Predominant corneal involvement rather than anterior chamber inflammation
Characteristic skin lesions in herpes zoster ophthalmicus

redFlags: Elevated intraocular pressure refractory to treatment
references: Jabs DA, Nussenblatt RB, Rosenbaum JT. Standardization of Uveitis Nomenclature for Reporting Clinical Data. Am J Ophthalmol. 2005.
Nussenblatt RB. The natural history of uveitis. Int Ophthalmol. 1990.
